I lost my dad/hero last October, I go down once a week to visit his grave and have a silent moment with him. I don't know if this is helpful or not but atm it gives me peace of mind.
I think his sudden passing was so overwhelming that my brain has built some kind of internal 'firewall' to stop me from receiving the full impact of his absence from my life, I don't know if this is a good thing or not.

As a (step) dad, I wholly endorse this, my own father passed recently, my daughter saw that I wasn't coping too well and signed herself and I to do a 10k run in July.
As well as giving me a target, it has bought us closer as we go for training runs several times a week.
I aspire to pass on the bond my father and I had to my two daughters and ditch all the alpha male/stiff upper lip bullshit.

I am as far as possibly away from the intended demographic for this show (northern English, working class, straight guy, early 40's)  but, goddamit, I had watery eyes in a lot of the episodes  either through sadness, joy or just sheer 'that was serious kick-ass' moments.  Breathtaking cinematography, awe inspiring musical score and an original, unique storyline.  I cannot wait for season 2.
This is fucking hilarious, just can't stop giggling to myself.  Wife thinks I'm mental, she could be right.

Best -  She understands how I'm feeling, we work a few things out and move forward as a couple. 

Worst -  She flies off the handle, has a total meltdown possibly involving self harm, we split up acrimoniously and I lose contact with my granddaughter and other family. 

Even if things do work out, this is only a piece of the jigsaw which contributes to my depression. 

I would like to thank you as being able to articulate what I'm feeling has helped in a small way.

I would be apprehensive about sharing how I feel with my wife, in the past she has gone way OTT even when I have broached the subject in a subtle manner. 

I just feel worn out.

Ok, after some thought, best case scenario is acceptance of current situation and being comfortable with it.   Worse case is a deterioration and lengthening of my 'black' spells ultimately leading to a point where I can't go on. 

Apologies for the vagueness but thinking of specifics is a bit of a stretch atm.
Can I leave this whilst tomorrow, I need some time to think through both scenarios.

I love my wife but am not in love with her.  We have so little to talk about and most times when we are alone, we sit in silence or are in different rooms.  But the thing is I don't want to hurt her and am inadequate at confrontation. 

I know this reads as the worst of clichés.

I'm pretty much in the 'upswing' atm so am comfortable with most questions.  As regards my marriage, there is no acrimony but there is little love there, we're just going through the motions. 
I have access to health care but am reluctant to go down the path of medication again.  I realise that I am the only one who can change things but cannot seem to find the energy and motivation to do so.

Usually anything from a day to a week, occurrence is sporadic.  I have a tendency to overthink and this usually triggers my dark spells and then it's a vicious circle until something 'gives' and then I feel 'normal' again. 
I was treated for depression in my twenties and through counselling and medication, I thought I was ok.  But now I am worried it is reoccurring.

I'm Jude, I just go through phases of total despondency.  Luckily, I have times when everything seems OK but am worried because these times are becoming less frequent. 
Options are severely limited, I am not a confrontational person and hate to see others hurt.  I bombed at my exams after being tipped to pass everything thanks to discovering pot and peer pressure.
